No. The evidence shows 81.3 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2021, or 2.23% of the 3,643.5-hectare property. Another 37.3 hectares of loss occurred in patches smaller than 0.5 hectares and was not counted as an event. Together, these areas represent about 3.3% of the property, not the whole property.

Most of the 81.3-hectare event area was mapped as planted pine forest; none was mapped as native forest. Tree-cover loss does not by itself establish the cause or whether the land was permanently cleared.
